title: Year 9 Science Test 1
topics: Biology (40%): variation, adaptation, natural selection, cells · Chemistry (20%): states of matter, atoms · Physics (40%)
weighting_note: Agreed with Albert, November 2026: the paper is split by time, 40% biology, 20% chemistry, 40% physics. At one mark a minute that is 16, 8 and 16 marks of the 40.
instructions: You have 40 minutes. There are three parts: Biology (16 marks), Chemistry (8 marks) and Physics (16 marks). Answer all the questions.
Spend about one minute on each mark: 16 minutes on Biology, 8 minutes on Chemistry and 16 minutes on Physics.
The last question in each part is harder (Stretch and Challenge). Answer the other questions in that part first.
Write your answers in the spaces on this paper. The marks for each part of a question are shown in brackets, for example [2].

sections.title: Part 1: Biology
sections.subject: biology
sections.intro: Questions 1 to 5 are Core. Question 6 is Stretch and Challenge.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Put one tick in each row to show whether the factor is abiotic (non-living) or biotic (living).
parts.answer: temperature: abiotic; predation: biotic; amount of light: abiotic; infectious disease: biotic. All four correct = 2 marks; two or three correct = 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Which one of these shows continuous variation? Tick one box.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the sentences using words from the box. One word is not needed.
gaps: Genetic information is stored in the ______________________ of a cell.
A sperm cell and an egg cell join together at ______________________ to make a zygote.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Draw one line from each way of protecting a species to how it works.

right: endangered animals are bred in captivity to increase their numbers
seeds, gametes or cells are stored at a low temperature
an area where the habitat and the species living in it are protected

parts.answer: nature reserve: an area where the habitat and the species living in it are protected; breeding programme: endangered animals are bred in captivity; gene bank: seeds, gametes or cells stored at a low temperature. All three correct = 2 marks; one correct = 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In the 1800s, black peppered moths became more common near Manchester. The sentences below explain why, but they are in the wrong order. Write 1, 2, 3 and 4 in the boxes to put them in the correct order.

rows: Birds spotted and ate more pale moths than black moths.
A few moths had genes that made them black.
Each generation had more black moths than the one before.
Soot from factories made the tree trunks black.

parts.answer: Correct order: a few moths had genes that made them black (1); soot made the tree trunks black (2); birds ate more pale moths (3); each generation had more black moths (4). All four correct = 2 marks; first and last correct = 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The diagram shows a plant cell. Write the name of each labelled part.
parts.answer: A cell wall, B nucleus, C chloroplast, D vacuole. All four correct = 2 marks; two or three correct = 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A microscope has a x10 eyepiece lens and a x4 objective lens. Calculate the total magnification.

questions.title: Natural selection in the Salton Sea

parts.label: a
parts.text: The Salton Sea in California has become saltier and saltier since 1905. Most fish species died out, but tilapia still live there and can cope with very salty water. Explain how natural selection made the tilapia able to live in very salty water.
parts.answer: By chance, some tilapia had genes (inherited variation) that helped them cope with salt (1). As the water got saltier, more of these fish survived than the others (1). They reproduced and passed on their genes (1), so each generation had more salt-tolerant fish, until all of them could cope (1). Do not credit 'the fish changed so they could cope'.

sections.title: Part 2: Chemistry
sections.subject: chemistry
sections.intro: Questions 7 and 8 are Core. Question 9 is Stretch and Challenge.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The diagrams show the particles in a solid, a liquid and a gas. Write solid, liquid or gas for each diagram.
parts.answer: A gas, B solid, C liquid. All three correct = 2 marks; one or two correct = 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A sodium atom has atomic number 11 and mass number 23.

sub.text: How many protons does the atom have?
How many neutrons does the atom have?

parts.label: b
parts.text: A sodium atom has 11 electrons. Complete its electron configuration.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Use your answer to part (b). Which group of the periodic table is sodium in? Tick one box.
parts.answer: group 1 (one electron in the outer shell).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Fluorine (atomic number 9) and chlorine (atomic number 17) are both in group 7 of the periodic table.

sub.text: Write the electron configuration of each atom.
Explain why fluorine and chlorine react in similar ways.

parts.answer: (i) fluorine 2,7 and chlorine 2,8,7, both correct (1). (ii) Both have seven electrons in the outer shell, and the outer electrons decide how an element reacts (1).
